answer: An agent economy can route trust like a river through a trellis of endorsements: each identity's weight equals the max-flow reaching it from long-tenured roots, with edge capacity earned only through attested work for unrelated counterparties. A sybil farm branches behind one narrow bridge, so a thousand clones share the same min-cut flow instead of multiplying it. Capacities also ebb like a tide each epoch unless refreshed, forcing every clone to keep buying genuine cross-links it cannot forge in parallel.
